stem:
Tendai Moyo owns a hardware shop in Chegutu. He does not keep a full set of books. At 1 January 2025 his assets and liabilities were: shop fittings US\$9,800, stock US\$7,840, debtors US\$3,260, rent prepaid US\$200, bank US\$2,280 and creditors US\$4,380.

A summary of his bank account for 2025:

| Receipts | US\$ | Payments | US\$ |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| Balance at 1 January 2025 | 2,280 | Creditors | 51,760 |
| Debtors | 61,420 | Wages | 7,590 |
| Cash sales (all banked) | ? | Rent | 2,520 |
|  |  | General expenses | 1,940 |
|  |  | Drawings | 6,500 |

Additional information at 31 December 2025:

1. Debtors were US\$3,840 and creditors US\$4,910. All purchases were on credit.
2. Stock was valued at US\$9,270.
3. Tendai sells all goods at a mark-up of 40% on cost. Sales are partly on credit and partly for cash; the cash sales figure was not recorded.
4. Rent of US\$280 was prepaid and general expenses of US\$135 were owing.
5. Shop fittings are to be depreciated at 10% per annum on cost.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the cost of sales for 2025.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Using the mark-up, calculate the total sales for 2025.

parts.label: (e)
parts.explanation: Credit sales (total debtors account) 61,420 + 3,840 − 3,260 = 62,000. Cash sales = 71,204 − 62,000 = 9,204.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Credit sales (total debtors account) 61,420 + 3,840 − 3,260 = 62,000. Cash sales = 71,204 − 62,000 = 9,204.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Prepare Tendai's income statement for the year ended 31 December 2025.

points.description: Correct heading (name, income statement, for the year ended 31 December 2025)
Sales 71,204 and cost of sales section 50,860 (own figures)

parts.explanation: Follow-through marks for own figures from (b)-(e).

parts.label: (g)
parts.explanation: 19,000 + net profit 7,259 − drawings 6,500 = 19,759. This agrees with net assets of 19,759.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 19,000 + net profit 7,259 − drawings 6,500 = 19,759. This agrees with net assets of 19,759.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Calculate the net profit percentage, to one decimal place.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: State **two** advantages to Tendai of keeping a full set of double-entry records.

points.description: A trial balance can be drawn up to check arithmetical accuracy
Sales, purchases and expenses are known directly, so missing cash or stock is easier to detect / figures accepted by lenders and ZIMRA

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: He could check his books with a trial balance, and he would know his cash sales and expenses exactly, so missing cash would be noticed at once.
